chapter: Lester Young and the early Basie years
title: Accepted by the Basie band; solos and the sacrifice of the big band
summary: Tate got solos but fewer than Prez, and would not make that sacrifice again.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Big band discipline versus small-group freedom

blocks.x: Let's go back to the Basie years.
You joined the band, you made it that night by playing --
Uh-huh. And the guys accepted you
Did Basie start assigning you solos?
Or did you just pick up Herschel's?

I played that. Then he started with the new arrangement, they started giving me solos. But never as many as he gave Prez. Well, I could understand that, you know, but actually, I thought that he should have given me more. But he didn't. So I just stayed there, you know, and I couldn't go through a thing now like I went through then, you know, in a big band, because I just couldn't -- if you don't play, you get so you can't play. You got to play all the time, you know, and I just wouldn't make a sacrifice like I made with Basie for any kind of money now. I'd rather play somewhere for just enough to get along and be able to play as often as I wanted to. As a matter of fact, I wouldn't want to work with a big band now, Gary. I like the way I do now.

But then, at the time, you know, I was glad to be with -- I was happy to be with the band and it was the big band era and we had a nice thing and I did get some things to play and I was raising a family and I needed the job.
